name: Rashi Peripherals Ltd (RPTECH)
tagline: India's #2 consumer-technology and components distributor with ~28% revenue CAGR - but a thin-margin distribution model structurally caps ROE at ~13%, so no 10x slope
business_overview: Rashi Peripherals (incorporated 1989) is India's second-largest distributor of consumer technology, embedded/semiconductor products and enterprise solutions - a pan-India network of 700+ locations, 57 branches, 50 service centres, 73 warehouses, 80 global brand partnerships (Intel, AMD, NVIDIA, Apple and others) and 10,250+ channel partners, organised into Personal Computing & Enterprise Solutions and Lifestyle & IT Essentials.
fundamentals_table: Low-margin, working-capital-intensive distribution; balance sheet described as adequate
fundamentals_narrative: Revenue growth is strong, but this is a distribution business: gross margins are thin, working capital is heavy, and ROE (~13%) reflects the structural economics of the model. Topline can compound with Indian IT-hardware demand, but the margin/return profile does not support a re-rating to multi-bagger valuations.

Not enough for a deep read. Filtered on business-model grounds: a thin-margin distributor with ~13% ROE does not clear the quality/upside bar even with ~28% revenue growth. Not in the old 108-stock project's tiers.

~28% revenue CAGR riding Indian PC, components and enterprise-hardware demand (incl. AI/GPU cycle)

verdict_headline: Fast-growing but structurally thin-margin distributor - filtered at the preliminary screen
verdict_reasoning: Strong revenue growth is offset by a distribution model that caps ROE near ~13% and carries heavy working capital - the quality/upside bar is not met
Not in the old 108-stock project. Conviction LOW, thesis-fit 'neither', no revisit
ValuePickr thread near-empty (3 posts) - no deep read; checkpoint set to the current highest post number

global_signal_check.signal_hypothesis: memory shortage shows up as optically higher revenue growth for the IT-hardware/memory distributor (Ishmohit's distributor thesis) - and/or margin expansion
global_signal_check.india_datapoint: Q1FY27 rev +61.9% YoY to Rs5,100cr; mgmt attributes 30-35% of growth to PRICE increases (memory/chip pass-through), 20-25% to volume, 5-10% to new brands; EBITDA margin CONTRACTED 24bps to 3.04% (mix shift to lower-margin PES); mgmt flagged an 'orange alert' on chip/memory component shortages that could cap future volume growth.
global_signal_check.note: Revenue leg of the distributor thesis is confirmed - the memory-price spike is optically inflating the topline exactly as predicted. But there is no margin benefit (thin ~3% distributor economics, margin actually down) and management frames the shortage as a forward volume HEADWIND, so this is not a clean positive same-signal read.

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: 'strong revenue growth is offset by a distribution model that caps ROE near ~13% and carries heavy working capital' - the distribution model itself is the structural constraint on differentiation (moat=no).
